revisit_notes: Analytic Tisserand/delta-max Saturn-frame model, not a time-dependent beam search. The single-moon caps are geometry (not phasing) dependent, so a phased tour cannot exceed them; the delta-max handoff bound shows the inner moons cannot pump vinf_T. A full Saturn-frame beam search (re-hosting trajectory-bot's heliocentric tour code) would only add tour DEPTH, not raise the per-moon escape cap -- it cannot beat Titan's 4.15 km/s.

Direction compounds the magnitude shortfall (not separately graded): the Titan-pumped Saturn-centric vinf points in a flyby-geometry-constrained direction that must then ADD to Saturn's heliocentric velocity in the RETROGRADE (sunward-dropping) sense for an Earth-return transfer. Even the 4.15 km/s magnitude would pay a cosine penalty to point correctly -- so 4.15 is an optimistic upper bound on the usable departure contribution.

vinf_T is Tisserand-conserved by TITAN flybys (the pump moon), so the arrival value 3.34 is a hard ceiling for Titan-only tours. Non-Titan pumping needs the inner moons, which turn <1 deg/flyby -- the round's decisive point.

B-ring taken at r=107,000 km (campaign R_RING). A lower harvest orbit (deeper) would give slightly higher vinf_T at Titan but also a deeper well to climb; the Titan cap is insensitive to it at the ~0.1 km/s level.

verdict.summary: The crack the ephemeris round opened is CLOSED and R186's Titan-lever revocation is CONFIRMED -- now with a derived Saturn-frame reason, not an asserted bound. The spacecraft harvests at the B-ring, and the minimal transfer to Titan fixes its Titan-relative excess at vinf_T = 3.34 km/s (reproducing R186's ~3.3 from first principles). Titan flybys conserve vinf_T, so a Titan-only tour caps the Saturn-centric departure excess at 4.15 km/s -- Titan is the sweet spot (inner moons are deeper and give less: Rhea 0.99, Tethys/Dione ~0; Iapetus far/slow at 3.41). Every moon needs more vinf than the B-ring provides (Titan closest, short by 0.67 km/s). The only way to pump vinf_T is a non-Titan handoff, but the inner moons turn the spacecraft <1 deg/flyby (mu 41-154 vs Titan's 8978) -- far too weak. So reaching the vinf_T=4.01 threshold requires propulsion, which is just supplying the departure energy the tour was meant to save. The 155-175 kWe reactor floor and bet #3 stand; the Titan 117 kWe branch stays dead. (Direction adds a further cosine penalty, so 4.15 is itself optimistic.)
